summary: An opinion article dated October 10, 2023 argues that local governments are lagging in adopting environmental policies that would strengthen local economies. It cites examples of green economy successes (Santa Monica, Greenfield, New Paltz, La Paz) and warns of the economic costs of inaction, including agricultural vulnerability, pollution-related healthcare costs, and lost green jobs and tourism. It calls on local leaders, grassroots groups and citizens to integrate economic and environmental policy.
one_line: A 2023 opinion piece argues local governments must adopt eco-friendly legislation to boost green jobs, renewable energy, and eco-tourism while avoiding the costs of environmental inaction.
key_facts: The article was written on October 10, 2023 and examines the link between environmental policy and local economic growth.
The green economy is described as practices and industries that spur economic growth while minimizing or reversing environmental impact.
Santa Monica, a coastal city, is cited as a pioneer in promoting green tech industries and incentivizing sustainable practices among local businesses.

Annie Hartford, an economist and environmental advocate, spoke at a forum on September 5, 2023 about 'triple bottom line' accounting, which measures social and environmental impact as well as profits.
As of September 22, 2023, Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed green jobs growing faster than average job growth in non-green sectors.
Dr. Marcella Reynolds, an epidemiologist, said on September 29, 2023 that respiratory illnesses linked to poor air quality have risen significantly, adding to local healthcare burdens.
Pollution such as smog or littering harms tourism, an important industry for many local economies.
The International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) released a report on October 1, 2023 stating renewable energy is now cost-competitive with, if not cheaper than, fossil fuels.
In Greenfield, renewable energy initiatives lowered utility costs for residents and businesses and attracted new investment.
New Paltz combined a stringent land use policy with ecotourism to build a robust, sustainability-oriented local economy with year-round tourists.
In La Paz, aggressive reforestation efforts and solar panel subsidies improved the local micro-climate and created new job sectors.
Extreme weather events attributed to climate change make agricultural sectors, the backbone of many rural economies, vulnerable.
